practices: Fresh shallows no longer add a crossing action; deep current still does.
Mud no longer adds routine step noise, though deep bogging still slows.
The first difficult cache recovery in a region earns one witnessed confidence.
Guarding on a damaged support seats one measure of bracing and cancels its warning.
Smoke leaves five paces of sight and inhalation clears sooner.
A laden pack does not add a second action on mud or shallow water.
A ranged weapon gains one pace from a higher level.
Known ice no longer causes poor footing; salt water remains open.
Digging a worked watercourse no longer needs a heavy tool.
Coastal rain, fog and squall leave one additional pace of sight.
Dry burning reeds and timber can be cut or extinguished without a heavy tool.
A lower-limb injury or heavy armour cannot both double a known upward climb.
Wet timber support can be braced without a levering tool.
A guarded reach weapon preserves one controlled reposition and presses morale.
Clay mud neither bogs the courier nor adds routine movement noise.
A committed weighted net remains as one physical recoverable bundle.
